## Written answers

Reproduced verbatim, including original spelling and grammar. Participants are identified by code only.

### Q12. Compared with the clip without vibration, did the vibration feedback change how you experienced the match?

**P01** — Not a big difference.

**P02** — I concentrated more. I had fewer distractions. But I noticed a slight mismatch in the timing

**P03** — Yes, the vibration can drag me into the exciting sports, can help me more concentrate. And the application can help me have the feel of my hand, it seems I'm in this match, it's more reality, more interesting.

**P04** — Much more engagement

**P05** — Yes, a little. I can feel that I am in the tennis game.

**P06** — More engaging

**P07** — The clip with vibration gave me the feeling of being a part of a game rather than only a viewer

**P08** — No. Because I prefer the visual experience.

**P09** — Definitely YES. I feel a part of the game when I watched the video with vibration.

**P10** — Yes, it helped me to find out easily whether they get the ball.

**P11** — I just wait the next vibration. and less focus on what the match displayed.

**P13** — It feels like playing by ourselves. Feels like I'm also holding the racket, and I will have the urge to swing my hands along.

**P14** — when I'm not focused vb helps me focused but when I'm focused vb distract me from watching  ["vb" = vibration]

**P17** — I was more engaged

**P18** — The game's points felt more noticeable with the haptic feedback and I got to focus more on the game rather than whether they hit the ball or not.

**P20** — Ya. I had to be strongly engrossed with the one without vibration. If I am busy and can't (as always) so felt it's useful

**P22** — It is great but holding the phone is tiresome. I would welcome another device.

### Q13. Did the vibration feedback feel natural or distracting? Why?

**P01** — It felt nature. no distracting.

**P02** — Not natural. But fun

**P03** — The vibration feel natural, not distracting. It give me feeling of myself match.

**P04** — Some time distracting. I may expect some response from the app

**P05** — Natural. Most of time it match the hit of the ball.

**P06** — Natural, difference between gentle hits and smash is a bit too small

**P07** — The vibration felt natural and I sensed the game better.

**P08** — Yes. Because the vibration feedback just reflected the hitting voice and didn't contain other information in the game.

**P09** — feels nature. It makes me feels like I am the on who play the game.

**P10** — Natural. The feedback is slight.

**P11** — distracting. my feeling just focus on my hand and I forget the content I watched (my eyes can't focusing at all)

**P13** — It's natural. I use the strongest mode already, but it's still not too strong because the vibration while I'm actually playing tennis is even stronger.

**P14** — half and half

**P17** — Initially I thought it would be distracting but I was surprised how engaged I was. I'm unsure if I would use it for watching every sporting event, however it would be interesting to know over an extended period of time

**P18** — It was unusual at first but I got used to it at the end.

**P20** — I felt it was good. and not distracting.

**P22** — natural. It's like using a playstation joystick.

### Q14. Any other comments or suggestions?

**P01** — A dummy racked would work better for me, and I prefer only feeling the vibration when one athlete hit the tennis.

**P02** — Synchronization can distort [transcription uncertain]. I think one time it missed a shot

**P03** — If the vibration's strength more stronger, it would be have more exciting feeling. The power of vibration can help viewer have more exciting feeling.

**P04** — the overall experience is better. It is better to produce higher level and longer time span of the vibration when the hit is stronger.

**P05** — It is a mobile app, so how to ensure during the video playing time avoid to others message or apps' notification vibration?

**P06** — phone is too big to hold.

**P07** — I guess, if the vibration matches more precisely with some movements like scoring a goal, or hitting the racket harshly from the competitor side, it would be more effective like you are riding on a roller coaster and when it goes up or down fast, you feel something in your heart. In some exciting moments of the game feeling the vibration would be enjoyable and exciting.

**P08** — No.

**P09** — It would be even better if the feedback on the hitting force could be provided.

**P10** — It'll be better if it report the result by different vibration

**P11** — I think I can not deal with (combinate) these two part of my body feeling at the same time without training.

**P13** — If the vibration could be even stronger, I would like it even more.

**P14** — vb has a limitation to express action because it moves for only ball touch. If it has different sequence could help  [transcription uncertain]

**P17** — The vibration feedback was in sync with what I was viewing.

**P18** — This haptic feedback was useful for when the sound was not very loud so I couldn't hear the points / the ball being hit.

**P20** — Maybe adding diff vibrations for each player. So that uk which team scored ["uk" = you know; transcription uncertain]

**P22** — Maybe another device so I am not tired after a few minutes of holding it.

## Caveats

- **P02 and P09 on Q3.** Recorded as *strongly disagree* for “I enjoyed the vibration feedback”, while also selecting *much more engaging* on Q10 and writing positive free-text. Either a participant mis-mark or an error reading the scan; check the paper originals before quoting Q3 on its own. No other conclusion depends on it.

- **P20 on Q8.** Recorded as *agree* for “the vibration feedback distracted me”, while answering the free-text question on exactly that point with “I felt it was good. and not distracting.” Either a participant mis-mark or an error reading the scan; check the paper originals before quoting Q8 on its own. No other conclusion depends on it.

- **P22 on Q10.** Recorded as *much less engaging* on Q10, while also selecting *strongly agree* on Q3 and writing that the feedback was “great” and felt natural. Either a participant mis-mark or an error reading the scan; check the paper originals before quoting Q10 on its own. No other conclusion depends on it.

- **Responses were transcribed by hand** from image-only scans; there is no text layer to verify against. Tick positions on 5-point rows are the most error-prone part.

- **Participant codes P12, P15, P16, P19, P21 are absent** from the returned forms. Codes were assigned at booking, so a gap most likely means a session that did not happen; confirm against the recruitment log.

- **The two clips were different footage.** Condition order was counterbalanced and is recorded, but which clip carried the haptics is not, so clip content is a potential confound on every experience item. The system-quality items (noticeable, fits, synchronised) are judgements about the haptics themselves and are far less exposed to it.

- **n = 17, convenience sample, nobody watches tennis more than monthly.** Enough to establish that the experience response is divided; not enough to explain who falls on which side.
